newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key U.S. T-bond sharply down by late Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: Key U.S. T-bond sharply down by late Tokyo trade.

text.p: The key 30-year U.S. Treasury bond fell sharply by late Tokyo trade on Wednesday on active speculative sales by dealers, traders said.

They said the market faced active selling pressure on a series of rumours and factors, including a report in the Wall Street Journal quoting traders, including a senior Goldman Sachs official, as questioning whether Japanese institutions will continue to buy U.S. Treasuries.
The key 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond dropped sharply to 99-24/32, yielding 6.52 percent, from New York's 100-4/32.

But one senior trader said the market should not overreact. "Whether Japanese institutional investors buy or not has very little significance in the Treasury market as Japanese participation has been very small," he said.

T-bond futures prices were also hammered down, with the March contract falling as low as 113-23/32 against a previous close of 114-12/32. Traders said falls in key December Globex S&P 500 stock futures traded on GLOBEX also hurt Treasuries.
"There are many rumours circulating. The market is very speculative. Worries that Wall Street might fall tonight were also a factor pushing prices down," another trader said.
